Structural axis exhausted: target proves identical ptr live-range yet opposite s0/s1 allocation + no 0+1 fold, so both remaining diffs are cc1-internal (global.c allocno-order tiebreak + cse2 const-pr

Structural axis closed in principle: ref-count re-weighting is inert (allocno_compare uses floor_log2, floor_log2(4)==floor_log2(6)) and type narrowing is inert; s0<->s1 swap + li/addiu fold remain cc
Permuter axis KILLED: ~11,700 iters over 2 faithful offset-0 chassis never touched the s0<->s1 swap or the li/addiu fold; lowest weighted score 98 (junk mutation), zero never approached.

Permuter axis re-confirmed dead on a 3rd distinct chassis (for/break, ~9546 iters, lowest 193, zero never approached, 13-diff never perturbed); structural+permuter axes all exhausted, next move is cc1

Forensics: cc1psx byte-identical to our fork on candidate.c (compiler-divergence escalation FORECLOSED); fold pinned to FIRST cse.c REG_WAS_0 const-prop, swap to global.c allocno-order; greg live-rang
Forensics: first-hand ALLOCDBG corrects s3/s6 numbers; counter(75) pri=17142 (nrefs=8,len=14) decisively beats pointer(74) pri=5882 (nrefs=5,len=17); fold-defeat entrenches (not flips) the swap.

frontier.hypothesis: The swap+fold are a byte-forced global.c+cse endgame-lock: with the emitted 33-insn stream fixing counter=(8 refs,len14) and pointer=(5 refs,len17), global.c deterministically gives the counter s0, and no single pure-C lever (incl. fold-defeat, which entrenches it) can flip it.
frontier.mechanism: allocno_compare pri=floor_log2(nrefs)*nrefs/livelen; counter 17142 vs pointer 5882 under fixed bytes. Fold-robust (barrier probe 22000 vs 5555).
frontier.next_probe: ESCALATION-modality session: this forensics session names/quantifies the passes; an escalation session files the OWNER-ESCALATION entry in docs/grind/decisions.md citing endgame-lock-disposition-policy + the s1-s7 measured-dead axes and this corrected first-hand ALLOCDBG attribution, then returns owner-gated.

frontier.hypothesis: A faithful count/pointer DECOMPOSITION that presents <=4 counter global.c allocno refs at the fixed 33-insn bytes (dropping counter pri below the pointer's 5882) AND places the entry ++ at a cse-block boundary would flip s0 to the pointer and match -- but the two requirements pull against each other (unfolding the entry ++ adds a counter ref).
frontier.mechanism: Only a source that redistributes allocno refs/live-lengths between the two pseudos WITHOUT changing the emitted instruction stream can differ from ours at global.c time -- the divergence is upstream of allocation, in the pre-alloc RTL shape.
frontier.next_probe: Only if the owner rejects escalation: structural search for a count that reads the counter through a distinct non-copy-propagated pseudo for the store/return (unlike s3's copy-propagated 'result'), reducing its allocno refs to <=4 while holding 33 insns.
